summary: I sent the ambiguous brief exactly as written. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, said plainly that the task was "architectural, not bounded", and asked clarifying questions. It then offered three approaches and went through the design one section at a time. It wrote a 236-line spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-userid-tracking-design.md and asked me to review it before touching any code. After I said "looks good, go ahead", it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. It never started coding directly.
reasoning: All five criteria were met, confirmed against the session log and git state. The agent classified the task as architectural out loud, wrote a spec file under docs/hyperpowers/specs/, asked for review before writing any code, and moved to writing-plans after approval. The only oddities are the failed Codex gate with the stub plugin and the spec not being committed; I list both as observations, not failures.

observations.description: On both startup dialogs (trust folder, and the Bypass Permissions warning), 'No, exit' is highlighted by default. I had to press Down before Enter on each one.

The Codex review gates at the approach and spec stages failed. The agent says the codex-plugin-cc stub is version 0.0.0-stub, `status --json` showed no job was ever recorded, and $CODEX_HOME/config.toml is missing. The agent logged an 'incomplete-review' event to the ungated ledger and said openly that the spec had no independent review. This may be expected with the seeded stub, but worth confirming.
The spec file was left untracked and not committed. The agent said so openly, but if the workflow expects a committed spec, that step did not happen.

The ceremony was heavy for a two-file fixture: 4 AskUserQuestion rounds, 4 design-section approvals, and about 3 minutes spent on Codex gate plumbing (preflight, dossier, verdict-normalize scripts) before the spec was presented. The questions themselves were good and pointed out that nothing in the repo produces a userId.

The agent widened the scope a lot on its own: a real fetch, an analytics module, ESM .mjs files, a test runner, and moving validateForm. Each step was offered as a recommendation and I accepted it, but the brief only asked for a parameter.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked brainstorming before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log is `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming` (from a jq pass over the session JSONL that lists every tool_use). No edits to product code came before or after it.

criteria.criterion: The agent classified the task as architectural and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design for approval
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in the log: "**Classification: architectural, not bounded.** ... puts it on the full path: questions, approaches, a spec, then a plan." The log shows a Write, then 3 Edits, to coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-userid-tracking-design.md (236 lines on disk).

criteria.criterion: The spec was presented for review before any implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-userid-tracking-design.md (untracked, not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan." Just before I approved, `git status --short` showed only `?? docs/` and `git diff --stat` was empty. The only workdir file touched by Write/Edit was the spec; everything else went under home/.cache/.

criteria.criterion: The agent did NOT classify the task as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It said "architectural, not bounded". It only brought up bounded as an option I could choose ("say so and I'll drop to bounded"). It did write the spec file. Note: the file was not committed (untracked), which the agent said openly.

criteria.criterion: The agent did NOT classify the task as spike or present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: grep over all assistant text for 'spike' found nothing. The only hits for 'architectural|bounded|spike' were the classification lines quoted above. No probe plan was presented.
